name: House Shot
description: Standard recreational house shot. Light oil concentrated in the middle with dry outside edges. Very forgiving and easy to score on.

name: Maxwell AFB House
description: Maxwell AFB bowling center standard house shot. Medium oil volume with slight taper. More challenging than a typical recreational house shot.

name: Maxwell AFB Tournament
description: Maxwell AFB tournament-style pattern. Heavier oil volume with shorter length creates demanding conditions requiring precise ball selection.

name: PBA Chameleon
description: Classic PBA animal pattern. Medium oil volume with a relatively even distribution. Considered the most bowler-friendly PBA pattern.
notes: Longest of the PBA animal patterns

name: PBA Cheetah
description: Short PBA animal pattern with light oil. The short length creates an early hook requiring urethane or polished reactive balls.
notes: Shortest PBA animal pattern — demands accuracy

name: PBA Viper
description: Challenging PBA animal pattern with medium oil and a tight window. Requires consistent ball speed and accurate targeting.

name: PBA Scorpion
description: Long PBA animal pattern with heavy oil. Requires a strong backend ball that can handle the distance before hooking.

name: PBA Shark
description: The most demanding PBA animal pattern. Very heavy oil volume requires maximum hook potential and precision.
notes: Hardest PBA animal — very heavy oil

name: Sport Shot
description: USBC Sport shot challenge. Heavier and more uniform oil distribution than a house shot, removing the built-in targeting aid.

name: US Open
description: One of the most difficult patterns in bowling. Extremely heavy oil with a very tight window for error. Only elite equipment and execution scores well.
notes: Considered the toughest major in bowling
